answers.answer: Keep 4 tokens of each gem color and all 5 gold tokens. Reveal 3 nobles; remove unrevealed nobles from the game permanently.
answers.evidence: Setup table: 2 players | 4 per color | 5 gold | 3 nobles. Setup: "Remove remaining noble tiles from the game -- they will not be used."

answers.answer: Three players use 5 gems per color, 5 gold and 4 nobles. Four players use 7 gems per color, 5 gold and 5 nobles: two more of each gem, unchanged gold and one more noble.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments by Player Count: 3 | 5 | 5 | 4; 4 | 7 | 5 | 5.

answers.answer: Shuffle each level separately. Place the decks in a column with level 1 at bottom, level 2 in the middle and level 3 on top. Reveal 4 cards from each level, giving 12 face-up cards in a 3x4 grid. The youngest player starts; play proceeds clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup: "Shuffle each ... separately"; "Level 1 at bottom, Level 2 in middle, Level 3 on top"; "Reveal 4 cards ... from each level." First Player: "The youngest player goes first. Play proceeds clockwise."

answers.answer: Choose exactly one: take 3 differently colored gems; take 2 same-colored gems if at least 4 are available beforehand; reserve a card if holding fewer than 3 reserved cards and receive a gold if available; or buy a face-up market card or previously reserved card. You cannot take gems and buy, or reserve and buy that card, in the same turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: "must perform exactly one" of four actions; purchase "1 face-up development card ... or 1 card you reserved on a previous turn."

answers.answer: All tokens you own must be visible to all players at all times.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: "All tokens a player owns must be visible to all players at all times."

answers.answer: Taking two green from four, leaving two, is allowed. Taking two red from three is not. Check the threshold before taking tokens. Neither gem-taking action allows gold.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: "at least 4 tokens in the supply before taking them"; both gem actions say "no gold". Take 2: "If a color pile has 3 or fewer tokens, you cannot take 2 from it."

answers.answer: Temporarily holding twelve is allowed. Return two tokens of your choice to finish at ten; these may include newly drawn gems. Gold counts toward the limit.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: "may temporarily exceed 10 during their action"; "return tokens of their choice ... exactly 10"; "some or all of the tokens they just took"; "including gold".

answers.answer: Take the available gold, temporarily reaching eleven tokens, then return one token of your choice, possibly that gold, to finish at ten. With an empty gold supply you may still reserve, receive no gold and remain at ten tokens.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card: "take 1 gold token"; "If no gold tokens remain, you may still reserve ... but receive no gold." Token Hand Limit allows temporary excess and returning gold obtained by reserving.

answers.answer: Reserve a face-up market card or the top card of any of the three level decks. Take a deck card without showing it to opponents. Only the player who reserved a card may buy it.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card: "A face-up development card from the 3x4 grid" or "The top card ... without revealing it"; "Reserved cards may only be purchased by the player who reserved them."

answers.answer: You cannot reserve a fourth card, even just to obtain gold. You cannot discard or exchange a reserved card to make room; purchasing it is the only way it can leave your hand.
answers.evidence: Reserved Cards: "If a player already has 3, they cannot reserve another"; "The only way to remove a reserved card from your hand is to purchase it."

answers.answer: Immediately refill the vacancy from the top of the level-2 deck. Purchasing a face-up card follows the same replacement rule. Buying a reserved card creates no market vacancy to refill. If the relevant deck is empty, leave the market space empty for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Card Replacement: "Whenever a face-up card is acquired (purchased) or reserved from the grid, it is immediately replaced by the top card of the same level's deck"; "If the corresponding deck is empty, the empty space ... remains empty for the rest of the game."

answers.answer: Spend one green token, or a gold replacing it; the two blue bonuses cover all blue cost. If bonuses cover every required color, spend no tokens. Bonuses are permanent and are not spent.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: "if a card costs 2 blue and 1 green, and you have 2 blue bonuses, you only need to spend 1 green token"; gold "can substitute for any single gem token"; enough bonuses permit buying "without spending any tokens at all." Bonus Stacking: bonuses are permanent.

answers.answer: Yes. After bonuses, the remaining cost is one blue, one black and one white. Spend your blue token for blue and your two gold for black and white. Return all three spent tokens to the supply. Keep your bonus cards and their permanent bonuses.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: bonuses reduce required tokens; gold "can substitute for any single gem token"; "Spend the required gem tokens, returning them to the supply"; "Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply." Bonus Stacking: bonuses are permanent.

answers.answer: Buy one face-up market development card or a previously reserved card from your hand. Arrange purchased cards face up in front of you, sorted by bonus color and staggered so bonuses and prestige point values are always visible to everyone.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card: "Purchase a face-up development card from the grid or a previously reserved card from your hand"; "sorted by bonus color and staggered so that bonuses and prestige point values are visible to all players at all times."

answers.answer: You do not qualify with only two white bonuses: neither a white token nor gold meets a noble requirement. Acquire a third white bonus and you qualify at the end-of-turn check. Bonuses above requirements do not disqualify you.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: "at least the quantity and types of bonuses"; "Noble visits require bonuses only (from cards), not gem tokens." Noble Tile Mechanics: "having more is fine."

answers.answer: Choose one noble. You cannot take both or decline all visits. The visit does not use another action and gives 3 prestige points. Check eligibility at the end of your turn after your action and the token-limit check.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: "cannot refuse it"; "not an action"; "choose one"; "at most one noble per turn"; "3 prestige points." Turn Structure: check "10-token hand limit and then ... noble visit."

answers.answer: Place the received noble tile face up in front of you.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: "Place the received noble tile face-up in front of you."

answers.answer: C and D still take their turns. A does not take another turn. B is not guaranteed to win because another player may finish the round with more prestige.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: "current round is completed so that every player has played the same number of turns." End-of-Game Clarifications: triggering player "may not necessarily win if another player surpasses them in the same final round."

answers.answer: Your new total is sixteen. This triggers the end condition because it applies at fifteen or more, including when skipping fifteen. Finish the current round so everyone has equal turns, then determine the winner from final scores and the tiebreaker if necessary.
answers.evidence: Noble tiles: "3 each." End-Game Trigger: "15 or more prestige points"; "current round is completed." Determining the Winner: "most prestige points at the end of the final round wins."

answers.answer: B wins. A and B tie at sixteen prestige, then B wins with nine purchased developments versus A’s ten. C has fewer prestige points, so its smaller card count does not help. Noble points count toward prestige. B’s three still-reserved cards are not purchased developments and do not count for the tiebreaker.
answers.evidence: Determining the Winner: "most prestige points" and "Noble tile points count toward the total." Tiebreaker: "fewest development cards" purchased. Reserved Cards: a reserved card leaves the hand only by purchase.
